### Task G — parameter-free constant-width CP vs the learned-scorer family

| mode | id_coverage | id_width | shift_coverage | shift_width |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| naive_matched | 0.895 | 4.067 | 0.901 | 3.345 |
| naive_no_scorer | 0.908 | 4.081 | 0.903 | 3.331 |
| dense | 0.882 | 4.584 | 0.896 | 4.354 |
| mvdf | 0.872 | 4.723 | 0.870 | 3.806 |


> `naive_no_scorer` = quantile of the 30% conformalize block only. `naive_matched` = quantile of train ∪ conformalize (80%), the SAME calibration data the learned modes get → budget-matched comparison.


- `naive_matched − dense` shift width **-1.009**, CI [-1.813, -0.252], sig 12/12, P(narrower)=1.00

- `naive_matched − mvdf` shift width **-0.461**, CI [-1.095, +0.097], sig 12/12, P(narrower)=0.94

- `naive_matched − naive_no_scorer  (budget sensitivity)` shift width **+0.015**, CI [+0.005, +0.024], sig 11/12, P(narrower)=0.00

- `naive_no_scorer − dense` shift width **-1.023**, CI [-1.821, -0.274], sig 12/12, P(narrower)=1.00

- `naive_no_scorer − mvdf` shift width **-0.475**, CI [-1.105, +0.081], sig 12/12, P(narrower)=0.95


**electricity shift coverage by seed (cf. mvdf 0.827 / 0.630 / 0.811):**

| mode | 0 | 1 | 2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| naive_matched | 0.894 | 0.895 | 0.894 |
| naive_no_scorer | 0.895 | 0.895 | 0.895 |


> **Budget audit resolved — CONFIRMS.** At the SAME 80% calibration budget the learned modes use, `naive_matched` reproduces the 30%-budget `naive_no_scorer` to within +0.015 shift width (P(narrower)=0.00, wrong sign for 'more data helps') — the calibration budget was doing nothing. `naive_matched` still beats every learned mode: −1.009 vs dense (12/12 sig, P=1.00), −0.461 vs mvdf (12/12). The FFDCI-style learned pinball scorer is not worth its parameters in ANY input space (dense / SAE-selected / SAE-random / PCA), and this is not a data-allocation artefact.
> The electricity coverage-*stability* pattern (naive_matched 0.894/0.895/0.894 by seed vs mvdf 0.827/0.630/0.811) holds at matched budget — the collapse is a learned-conditioning artefact. Does not touch H1c or H3.


### Task A — traffic ID coverage anomaly

traffic ID coverage = 1.000 on 24/24 runs (all 8 modes x 3 seeds) -> **structural, not seed noise, not mode-specific.**


**H6 split sizes (E_eval_ID -> 50/30/20 chronological):**

| dataset | test_windows | E_eval_ID | mlp_train | conformalize | id_width_eval |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ETTh1 | 5900 | 1966 | 983 | 589 | 394 |
| ETTh2 | 5900 | 1966 | 983 | 589 | 394 |
| electricity | 7000 | 2334 | 1167 | 700 | 467 |
| traffic | 3509 | 1169 | 584 | 350 | 235 |


> **Root cause:** E_eval_ID split CHRONOLOGICALLY; traffic's E_eval_ID is 1169 windows (vs ~1966 ETT, ~2334 electricity) - too short for the conformalize block (middle 30%) to characterize the disjoint ID-width-eval block (last 20%) under traffic's strong daily/weekly cycle. q_resid over-covers -> ID coverage 1.000, ID width inflated (~11 vs shift ~8). The online ACI term adapts q down on the shift block (shift coverage ~0.91, near nominal).
> **Resolution:** traffic H6 row is **directional only** - the shift-width ranking (mvdf/correlated/random_k < dense < pca_k) matches the other 3 datasets, but the scorer is not tightly ID-calibrated on traffic at this split budget. Flagged, not dropped. A proper fix needs a larger E_eval_ID (out of scope this phase).


### Task B — electricity `mvdf` shift undercoverage

**electricity shift coverage by mode x seed:**

| mode | 0 | 1 | 2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| naive_matched | 0.894 | 0.895 | 0.894 |
| naive_no_scorer | 0.895 | 0.895 | 0.895 |
| dense | 0.878 | 0.875 | 0.875 |
| mvdf | 0.827 | 0.630 | 0.811 |
| dense+mvdf | 0.879 | 0.879 | 0.877 |
| correlated | 0.833 | 0.839 | 0.837 |
| random_k | 0.839 | 0.744 | 0.818 |
| pca_k | 0.878 | 0.867 | 0.866 |


> **Findings:** (1) NOT mvdf-only - `random_k` also drops (seed 1: 0.744). All three sparse-SAE-subset modes (mvdf/correlated/random_k, ~4-9% feature activation) lose more shift coverage than dense/pca_k. (2) **seed 1 is the outlier** (mvdf 0.630 vs seeds 0/2 at 0.827/0.811). (3) 47-vs-48-channel quirk ruled out - feature indices are SAE latent dims (0-2047), not channels; the channel path is identical for all modes. (4) Consistent with the H3 sparse-activation story.
> **Resolution:** report `mvdf`'s electricity shift-width advantage (23%) WITH its coverage cost inline (mean shift coverage 0.756 vs dense 0.876). Does not change the H6 conclusion (all three sparse modes show the same shift-width benefit); qualifies electricity specifically.

- Aggregate paired bootstrap: mean **-0.138**, 95% CI [-0.309, -0.016], P(mvdf<random_k) = 1.00

**Per-dataset Delta_d = mean_s(W_mvdf - W_random_k), shift width:**

| dataset | Delta_d | direction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ETTh1 | -0.008 | mvdf narrower |
| ETTh2 | 0.007 | mvdf WIDER |

> **Direction:** `mvdf` narrower than `random_k` under shift on aggregate (mean -0.138) and on 3/4 datasets by Delta_d. BUT ETTh1/ETTh2 magnitudes are tiny (~0.01 on a 2-3 wide interval) and the electricity/traffic advantages coincide exactly with `mvdf`'s coverage drops there (Task B; traffic Task A). **Write-up wording: selection has a small residual effect on top of the basis effect, confounded with coverage on the two datasets where it is non-trivial, and reversed on ETTh2.**
> **Freeze-doc Task D gate** needs POST-coverage-fix data. On this PRE-fix data, rule (a) holds (CI [-0.309, -0.016]) and rule (b) holds (3/4) - but the coverage confound blocks certification. Provisional: **MVDF-default IF the coverage fix preserves the direction; else cheap-default (`correlated`).**
